channelGuide.discord.bot_token.descripti: Create an application in the Discord developer portal, add a bot, and paste its token. People reach the bot by direct message; it needs no public URL.
channelGuide.discord.bot_token.field.tok: Developer portal › your application › Bot › Reset Token. Whoever has it controls the bot.
channelGuide.discord.bot_token.label: Bot token
channelGuide.discord.bot_token.step.crea: In the Discord developer portal, choose New Application and give it a name.
channelGuide.discord.bot_token.step.past: Paste the token below and connect. The bot keeps its own connection to Discord, so no public address is needed.
channelGuide.discord.bot_token.step.serv: Discord lets people message a bot only when they share a server with it. After connecting, add the bot to a server they are in.
channelGuide.discord.bot_token.step.toke: Open Bot and press Reset Token, then copy the token. No privileged intent is needed: the bot reads only direct messages.
channelGuide.discord.description: One Discord bot per connection. People talk to it in direct messages; server channels and threads are ignored.
channelGuide.slack.description: One Slack app per connection, installed in one Slack workspace; people message the Bot in the app's direct messages.
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.descripti: Create a Slack app with Socket Mode and the Messages tab on, subscribe it to the message.im bot event, give the bot the chat:write, im:history, files:read and users:read scopes, install it in your Slack workspace, then paste its bot token and an app-level token with connections:write.
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.field.app: Basic Information › App-Level Tokens, with the connections:write scope. It starts with xapp-.
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.field.bot: Install App › Bot User OAuth Token. It starts with xoxb-.
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.label: Slack app (Socket Mode)
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.step.app_: Open Basic Information, App-Level Tokens: generate a token with the connections:write scope and copy it (xapp-…).
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.step.crea: Create a Slack app: choose From a manifest, pick the Slack workspace people will use, and paste the app manifest below. Rename the app if you like.
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.step.inst: Open Install App, install the app in the workspace, and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…).
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.step.mess: In Slack, open the app under Apps and write to it on its Messages tab.
channelGuide.slack.socket_mode.step.past: Paste both tokens below and connect. Slack delivers messages over Socket Mode, so no public address is needed.
channelGuide.telegram.description: One Telegram bot per connection, answered by one Deskmates bot. Private chats only; text and images in, text replies out.
channelGuide.telegram.token.description: Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Each Deskmates bot needs its own Telegram bot. People must open the bot and press Start before it can reply.
The token BotFather sent, like 123456789:AA…. Whoever has it controls the bot; Deskmates stores it encrypted and never shows it again.
channelGuide.telegram.token.label: Bot token
channelGuide.telegram.token.step.name: Choose a display name and a username that ends in bot. BotFather answers with the bot's token.
channelGuide.telegram.token.step.one_bot: Use a new Telegram bot for each Deskmates bot: one Telegram bot is answered by exactly one Deskmates bot.
channelGuide.telegram.token.step.paste: Paste the token below and connect. Deskmates asks Telegram for new messages itself, so no public address is needed.
channelGuide.telegram.token.step.start: Open the bot in Telegram and press Start. Telegram lets a bot reply only to people who started it.
channelGuide.wechat.description: Scan with WeChat to connect one account to one Deskmates bot. Private text conversations only.
channelGuide.wechat.qr.description: Choose a bot, connect, then scan the QR code with WeChat and confirm on your phone.
channelGuide.wechat.qr.label: Scan with WeChat
channelGuide.wechat.qr.step.account: Use a WeChat account eligible for iLink. Each connected account is answered by exactly one Deskmates bot.
channelGuide.wechat.qr.step.message: Send a private text message from WeChat to check the reply. Groups, images, voice and files are not supported in this version.
channelGuide.wechat.qr.step.relink: If authorization expires, link the same account again. Disconnect here stops synchronization; remove authorization in WeChat to revoke it there.
channelGuide.wechat.qr.step.scan: Choose the bot and connect below. Scan the QR code with WeChat and confirm authorization on your phone.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.description: Use a Meta Business phone number and signed webhooks.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.field.access: A system user's permanent token with whatsapp_business_messaging.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.field.appSec: App settings › Basic in your Meta app. Deskmates uses it to check that webhooks come from Meta.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.field.graphA: Leave it empty to use v23.0.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.field.phoneN: WhatsApp › API Setup in your Meta app. It is a long number, not the phone number itself.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.field.verify: The same text you enter in Meta's webhook settings.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.label: Business Cloud API
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.step.app: In Meta for Developers, create a Business app and add the WhatsApp product.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.step.number: Under WhatsApp, API Setup, copy the Phone number ID of the number that should answer.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.step.secret: Under App settings, Basic, copy the App secret.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.step.token: In Business settings, create a system user with the whatsapp_business_messaging permission and generate a permanent access token for it.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.step.verify: Make up a verify token: any long random text. Enter it below and in Meta's webhook settings.
channelGuide.whatsapp.cloud.step.webhook: Under WhatsApp, Configuration, set the Callback URL to this Deskmates server's public address followed by the path below, enter the verify token, and subscribe to the messages field.
channelGuide.whatsapp.description: Connect one WhatsApp account to one default Bot.
channelGuide.whatsapp.qr.description: Scan a QR code from WhatsApp Linked devices.
Only when this server must reach WhatsApp through a proxy. Leave it empty otherwise.
channelGuide.whatsapp.qr.label: QR linked device
channelGuide.whatsapp.qr.step.number: Pick the WhatsApp account that should answer. Messages to its number reach the chosen bot, so use a number meant for this rather than a personal one.
channelGuide.whatsapp.qr.step.phone: On that phone, open WhatsApp, then Linked devices (in Settings on iPhone, in the ⋮ menu on Android), and choose Link a device.
channelGuide.whatsapp.qr.step.scan: Press Connect here and scan the QR code that appears. The phone stays the account's main device and must keep its internet connection.
integrations.accounts.title: Connected accounts
integrations.adopted: {name} adopted; its actions are now offered to runs.
integrations.apps.adoptedOnly: Showing adopted apps only because the full list could not be loaded. Refresh to try again.
integrations.apps.allConnected: Every app enabled here is already connected. Search to find another one.
integrations.apps.howBotsUse: Bots in this workspace use connected apps without seeing a key. Reading runs without asking; anything that changes data asks for approval first.
integrations.apps.includeNotEnabled: Include apps not enabled on this installation
integrations.apps.label: Apps
integrations.apps.listUnreadable: Apps could not be loaded. Refresh to try again; if it still fails, ask the person who runs Deskmates to check the integration service.
integrations.apps.noProviders: The integration service has no apps yet. Ask the person who runs Deskmates to add one, then refresh.
integrations.apps.noneEnabled: No app is enabled on this installation yet. Search to see what the integration service offers, and ask the person who runs Deskmates to enable one.
integrations.apps.tabIntro: Services your Bots can use while they work, such as email, documents and code. Connect an account once; every Bot in this workspace can then use it.
integrations.apps.unconfigured: Apps are not available on this server yet. Ask the person who runs Deskmates to connect the integration service, then refresh this page.
integrations.botChannels.title: Chat channels
integrations.categories.label: Integration categories
integrations.channels.admissionChanged: Every sender is now admitted. {channel} no longer uses a list of allowed senders: anyone who messages this account reaches its Bot and can answer the approvals of their own chat. The earlier list was removed and nobody was blocked. Block a number below to keep it out.
integrations.channels.explain.archived: This workspace is in Trash, so this connection is stopped. Its link and settings are kept; restoring the workspace starts it again.
integrations.channels.explain.disconnect: Deskmates cannot reach this account right now. Select Retry; if it keeps failing, disconnect and connect again.
integrations.channels.explain.noBot: Add a Bot to this workspace first: every conversation on this channel goes to one default Bot.
integrations.channels.explain.reconnect: The account signed out. Select Reconnect, or disconnect and connect again with new details.
integrations.channels.explain.relink: The phone unlinked this device, or the saved link is no longer valid. Select Link again and scan the new QR code.
integrations.channels.loadFailed: Channel status could not be loaded. Try again; if it still fails, ask the person who runs Deskmates to check the server.
integrations.channels.menu.explain: Only the selected scope and language are inspected or replaced. Other overrides cannot be enumerated; repeat for known chat IDs and languages. For default/private scope, button replacement affects the default button. Connecting or restarting never changes menus.
integrations.channels.menu.language: Language code (two lowercase letters; empty for fallback)
integrations.channels.menu.replace: Replace the target menu button with commands, including a custom Web App button
integrations.channels.menu.title: Command menu
integrations.channels.roleNote: connect or change a chat channel
integrations.channels.scanQr: Scan this code in WhatsApp to link the account.
integrations.channels.tabIntro: Let people talk to your Bots from apps they already use. Each account on a channel is answered by one Bot, and its conversations also appear under Chats.
integrations.channels.unavailable.body: Ask the person who runs Deskmates to update or restart it so the built-in channels can load. Nothing on this page needs to be set up first.
integrations.channels.unavailable.saved: Your saved connection is kept and resumes when its channel is available again.
integrations.channels.unavailable.title: Chat channels are not available on this server right now.
integrations.channels.v2.blocklistExplai: Anyone can message this account. Messages from people on this list are ignored, and nothing more is sent to them.
integrations.channels.v2.rebindExplain: Conversations so far stay with {bot} as read-only history. New messages go to the Bot you choose, and each person is told once that a different assistant now answers.
integrations.channels.v2.rebindNoOther: Add another Bot to this workspace to switch to it.
integrations.channels.v2.relinkExplain: Use new credentials for the same account. A different account must be connected as a new connection.
integrations.connect.description: Connect an account for this workspace. Give additional accounts a different name.
integrations.connect.driveAccess: Connecting Google Drive grants file access separately from signing in to Deskmates or another app with Google.
integrations.connect.name: Connection name
integrations.connect.nameHelp: A short name Bots use to pick this account, such as main or sales.
integrations.connect.oauthNotice: Finish the grant in the new tab, then refresh this list.
integrations.connect.oauthUnavailable: Sign-in connection is not available on this server. Use an API key, or ask the person who runs Deskmates to enable it.
integrations.connect.title: Connect {name}
integrations.database.description: Connect a PostgreSQL-compatible database without exposing its address or credential to Bots. Each submitted batch returns a receipt.
integrations.database.name: Name
integrations.database.title: Register a database
integrations.databases.addIntro: Register the database connection with its address and credential. The server stores both securely and never gives them to Bots.
integrations.databases.intro: Receipted connectors: every submission is validated, run once and receipted.
integrations.databases.label: Databases
integrations.databases.usage: A Bot names {name} in its connectors list to use it.
integrations.intro.named: How people reach {workspace}'s Bots, and what the Bots can use beyond the browser. Credentials never enter the workspace.
integrations.intro.unnamed: How people reach the workspace's Bots, and what the Bots can use beyond the browser. Credentials never enter the workspace.
integrations.next.connectApp: connect an account of an app that is ready to connect
integrations.noWorkspace: Choose a workspace to see its connections.
integrations.search.label: Search all apps
integrations.search.placeholder: Search all apps, such as Gmail or GitHub
integrations.setup.approvals: When a Bot needs approval, it asks in that chat; you can also answer in Approvals.
integrations.setup.failed: Not connected: {error}. Check the details and try again; nothing was saved.
integrations.setup.oneBot: Everyone who messages this account talks to this Bot. You can switch to another Bot later.
integrations.setup.title: Connect {name}
integrations.setup.whereChats: Message the account on {name} to start. Each conversation also appears under Chats here, read-only: reply from {name}.
